title: Logarithmic differential coordinates and derivations from strict infinitesimal lifting
statement:
Let $f:(X,M)\to(Y,N)$ be a morphism of locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], with underlying map locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A fine log structure on an arbitrary scheme means the same sheaf-of-commutative-monoids log structure, admitting etale-local charts by finitely generated integral monoids, without requiring saturation or a Noetherian underlying scheme. Suppose that every commutative square of fine log schemes over $f$, whose left arrow $i:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ is a first order thickening [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] and is strict (the log structure on $T_0$ is the associated log structure of the inverse image of that on $T$), admits log lifts etale locally on $T$ [def-weil-etale-morphism]. This lifting hypothesis is preserved on replacing $X$ and $Y$ by compatible etale neighbourhoods with pulled-back log structures.

Define $\omega_f$ on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] to be the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the module generated by $da$ for functions and $d\log m$ for log sections, modulo additivity of $d$, $d(ab)=a\,db+b\,da$, $d\log(mm')=d\log m+d\log m'$, $d\alpha(m)=\alpha(m)d\log m$, and $dc=d\log n=0$ for functions and log sections from $Y$. Then $\omega_f$ is finite locally free: etale locally on $X$ it is $\mathcal O_X^r$ for some finite $r$. At each geometric stalk [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] there are $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in M_{\bar x}$ such that $d\log t_1,\ldots,d\log t_r$ form a basis; these sections and their basis property extend to a pointed etale neighbourhood.

For any of the strict test thickenings with ideal $\mathcal I$, fixed $a_0:T_0\to X$ and $b:T\to Y$, the sheaf of log lifts on $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$ is a torsor under $\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_{T_0}}(a_0^*\omega_f,\mathcal I)$. Explicitly a homomorphism is a pair $(D,\delta)$ with $D$ a relative derivation of functions into $\mathcal I$, $\delta:a_0^{-1}M^{\rm gp}\to\mathcal I$ an additive homomorphism killing the image of $N^{\rm gp}$, and $D(\alpha(m))=a_0^*(\alpha(m))\delta(m)$. It changes a lift by $a^\sharp(c)\mapsto a^\sharp(c)+D(c)$ and $a^\flat(m)\mapsto a^\flat(m)(1+\delta(m))$. Every pair of lifts differs by exactly one such homomorphism. Here $a_0^*\omega_f=\mathcal O_{T_0}\otimes_{a_0^{-1}\mathcal O_X}a_0^{-1}\omega_f$ and $1+\mathcal I$ is identified with the additive ideal since $\mathcal I^2=0$. If every test square has exactly one global log lift, then $\omega_f=0$.

source.place: Expose X Proposition 1.2 proof, printed pp.136–138, and XVI Proposition 3.6.3 proof, printed p.252, contextual references to Kato. Precise input: Kato, Logarithmic structures of Fontaine–Illusie, Propositions 3.9–3.10 and proof 3.13, printed pp.203–204 (WANTED locally; primary source read online).

proof.text: First check the localization assertion. Let $X'\to X$ and $Y'\to Y$ be compatible etale neighbourhoods with pulled-back log structures. Compose a test square for $X'/Y'$ with $X\to Y$ and use the assumed local log lift into $X$. By [def-weil-etale-morphism], $X'\to X$ is flat and unramified. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-unramified-formally-etale] on affine pieces of the test thickening to lift its given $T_0\to X'$ uniquely over the lift into $X$. The two resulting maps into $Y'$ agree: they lift the same map from $T_0$ over $Y$, and $Y'\to Y$ has the same uniqueness property. Since the log structures on $X',Y'$ are pulled back, the associated-log universal property in [lem-sfb-fine-chart-logification-thickening] extends these scheme maps to the required log maps; their equality on charts gives compatibility over $Y'$. Thus the lifting hypothesis remains true after this localization.

source.place: Kato 3.2 and the etale-local convention in 3.3; ILO X Proposition 1.2 proof, pp.136--138; precise Kato source WANTED locally, read online at https://math.uchicago.edu/~drinfeld/p-adic_periods/Kato_log-structures.pdf

proof.text: The displayed relations defining $\omega_f$ give the following universal property directly. A map from $a_0^{-1}\omega_f$ to an $\mathcal O_{T_0}$-module $J$ assigns $da\mapsto D(a)$ and $d\log m\mapsto\delta(m)$. It factors through the relations exactly when $D$ is a relative derivation, $\delta$ is additive on $a_0^{-1}M^{\rm gp}$ and zero on the base log group, and $D(\alpha(m))=a_0^*(\alpha(m))\delta(m)$. A monoid homomorphism to an additive group extends uniquely to the group completion by $\delta(m/m')=\delta(m)-\delta(m')$. The module-sheafification universal property [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface], together with [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and tensor adjunction identify these pairs with $\mathcal O_{T_0}$-linear maps $a_0^*\omega_f\to J$. This is a computation with the defining generators and relations, not an appeal to a smoothness criterion.

source.place: Kato 1.7, pp.195--196, and 3.9, p.203; ILO XVI 3.6.3 proof, p.252; precise Kato source WANTED locally, read online at https://math.uchicago.edu/~drinfeld/p-adic_periods/Kato_log-structures.pdf

proof.text: Use [sbc-lem-thickening-etale-site] to identify the etale sheaves on the test thickening and its reduction. In particular the inverse images along the two lifts restrict to the fixed inverse image along $a_0$, so they can be compared under this equivalence. For any strict test thickening and any two log lifts $a,a'$, put $D(c)=a'^\sharp(c)-a^\sharp(c)$. This lies in $\mathcal I$, vanishes on base functions, and expansion of the two products gives $D(cd)=a_0^*(c)D(d)+a_0^*(d)D(c)$ because $\mathcal I^2=0$. Work locally in an integral chart for the test log structure. The strict-thickening assertion of [lem-sfb-fine-chart-logification-thickening] gives a unique $\delta(m)\in\mathcal I$ with $a'^\flat(m)=a^\flat(m)(1+\delta(m))$. Multiplicativity, together with $(1+u)(1+v)=1+u+v$, makes $\delta$ additive, hence a homomorphism on the group completion. The lifts agree over $Y$, so $\delta$ kills its base log sections. Compatibility with the structural map gives $D(\alpha(m))=a_0^*(\alpha(m))\delta(m)$. The local differences agree on overlaps by uniqueness, hence define one global pair. Step 2 identifies it with exactly one homomorphism from $a_0^*\omega_f$.

source.place: Kato Proposition 3.9, p.203; ILO XVI 3.6.3 proof, p.252; precise Kato source WANTED locally, read online at https://math.uchicago.edu/~drinfeld/p-adic_periods/Kato_log-structures.pdf

proof.text: Conversely, for a pair $(D,\delta)$ of Step 2 and a lift $a$, the formulas $a'^\sharp(c)=a^\sharp(c)+D(c)$ and $a'^\flat(m)=a^\flat(m)(1+\delta(m))$ define a lift. The derivation identity proves multiplicativity of the ring map, and additivity of $\delta$ proves multiplicativity of the monoid map. The mixed relation proves compatibility with $\alpha$; the vanishing base relations prove that it is over $Y$. These maps reduce to the old ones since $D,\delta$ take values in $\mathcal I$. The chart universal property in [lem-sfb-fine-chart-logification-thickening] supplies the associated log maps and their uniqueness. The construction and Step 3 are inverse. Scheme maps glue on etale covers by [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf], and morphisms of log sheaves glue by the sheaf condition on their values. Thus the lift functor is a sheaf; the assumed local existence and the simply transitive action just proved make it the asserted torsor.

source.place: Kato Proposition 3.9, p.203; ILO XVI 3.6.3 proof, p.252; precise Kato source WANTED locally, read online at https://math.uchicago.edu/~drinfeld/p-adic_periods/Kato_log-structures.pdf

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-log-differential-finite-chart-model], using local Noetherianity, fineness of the log structures, and local finite presentation of the underlying map. Around a fixed geometric point choose its affine chart neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ over $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and its finitely presented model $W$ for $\omega_{U/V}$. Step 1 permits use of the lifting hypothesis for $U/V$, and the etale comparison in that node identifies its differential sheaf with the restriction of $\omega_f$. Choose a finite surjection $\pi:E=A^n\twoheadrightarrow W$ and write $K=\ker\pi$. We will split $\pi$ after an etale neighbourhood of the chosen point, rather than assuming that finite presentation alone implies freeness.

source.place: Kato 2.1, p.197, and Proposition 3.10, p.203; ILO XVI 3.6.3 proof, p.252; precise Kato source WANTED locally, read online at https://math.uchicago.edu/~drinfeld/p-adic_periods/Kato_log-structures.pdf

proof.text: Use the square-zero rings of [def-sc-trivial-square-zero-extension]. For each $A$-module $J$, put $T_J=\operatorname{Spec}(A\oplus J)$ and give it the log structure associated to the chart $P\to A\oplus J$, $p\mapsto(\alpha(p),0)$. This is a fine integral log structure by [lem-sfb-fine-chart-logification-thickening]. The quotient $A\oplus E\twoheadrightarrow A\oplus W$ gives a strict first order thickening $T_W\hookrightarrow T_E$ with ideal $0\oplus K$: products of any two infinitesimals vanish. The projections $T_J\to U$ give canonical log maps $c_J$ over $V$. By Step 2 the identity of $W$ gives the universal log derivation $(d,d\log)$ into $W$. Apply the action of Step 4 to $c_W$ for the thickening $U\hookrightarrow T_W$. It yields a log map $a_0:T_W\to U$ with $a_0^\sharp(a)=(a,da)$ and $a_0^\flat(m)=c_W^\flat(m)(1+d\log m)$. This is over $V$, since both universal differentials vanish on the base. Hence $a_0$, $T_W\hookrightarrow T_E$, and $T_E\xrightarrow{c_E}U\to V$ form a test square covered by the hypothesis.

source.place: Kato Proposition 3.10 reduced to 3.9, p.203; explicit square-zero test expanding the omitted classical argument; precise Kato source WANTED locally, read online at https://math.uchicago.edu/~drinfeld/p-adic_periods/Kato_log-structures.pdf

proof.text: The lifting hypothesis gives a lift of $a_0$ etale locally on $T_E$. The nilpotent invariance [sbc-lem-thickening-etale-site], applied to $U\hookrightarrow T_E$, identifies this covering locally with the base changes of an affine etale cover $\operatorname{Spec}B\to U$. Indeed the canonical base change of any such $B$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] and has coordinate ring $B\otimes_A(A\oplus E)=B\oplus E_B$, where $E_B=B\otimes_AE$; full faithfulness in nilpotent invariance identifies it with the corresponding etale object over $T_E$. On one such neighbourhood meeting the chosen point, compare a lift $a$ with $c_E$. They coincide on $\operatorname{Spec}B\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}(B\oplus E_B)$. Steps 2--4, now for the ideal $E_B$, give a $B$-linear map $s:W_B\to E_B$. Reducing this difference along $E_B\to W_B$ gives the difference between $a_0$ and $c_W$, which is the identity universal derivation by Step 6. Its values on $da$ and $d\log m$ therefore give $\pi_Bs=\mathrm{id}_{W_B}$. The tensor description of $W_B$ is precisely the one in [lem-sfb-log-differential-finite-chart-model].

source.place: Kato Proposition 3.10 reduced to 3.9, p.203; nilpotent neighbourhood comparison: Stacks Tag 03SI; precise Kato source WANTED locally, read online at https://math.uchicago.edu/~drinfeld/p-adic_periods/Kato_log-structures.pdf

proof.text: Thus $W_B$ is a direct summand of $E_B=B^n$: explicitly $e=s\pi_B(e)+(e-s\pi_B(e))$ separates the summands $s(W_B)$ and $\ker\pi_B$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover] to obtain a Zariski open cover of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ on which $W_B$ is finite free. The tensor model and etale comparison of [lem-sfb-log-differential-finite-chart-model] identify these free modules with the restrictions of $\omega_f$. Since every chosen geometric point lies on such a neighbourhood, $\omega_f$ is finite locally free on the small etale site.

source.place: Kato Proposition 3.10, p.203; Stacks Tag 00NX, lemma-finite-projective, (3) implies (7); ILO XVI 3.6.3 proof, p.252; precise Kato source WANTED locally, read online at https://math.uchicago.edu/~drinfeld/p-adic_periods/Kato_log-structures.pdf

proof.text: Fix a geometric point in the rank-$r$ free neighbourhood of Step 8. The underlying abelian sheaf of the module sheafification is the abelian sheafification by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface]; [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-geometric-stalk] therefore represents each stalk element by the local differential generators and relations. For any function $a$ on an affine pointed neighbourhood, either $a$ or $1+a$ has nonzero image at the marked point. Restricting to its principal open makes that element a unit. In the first case $da=a\,d\log a$; in the second case $da=d(1+a)=(1+a)d\log(1+a)$. Units are log sections by [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Thus dlogs of actual monoid sections span the geometric differential fibre. In its $r$-dimensional residue vector space choose $r$ such images forming a basis, say $d\log t_1,\ldots,d\log t_r$ with $t_i\in M_{\bar x}$. If $r=0$, take the empty family. This uses no characteristic or division assumption on the base.

source.place: Kato 1.7, pp.195--196, and 3.13, p.204; ILO XVI 3.6.3 proof, p.252; precise Kato source WANTED locally, read online at https://math.uchicago.edu/~drinfeld/p-adic_periods/Kato_log-structures.pdf

proof.text: Represent the finite family $t_i\in M_{\bar x}$ by actual log sections on one pointed etale neighbourhood; the pointed-neighbourhood colimit defining the stalk [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] and cofilteredness [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered] give a common refinement of the finitely many representatives. Restrict further to an affine neighbourhood on which Step 8 has already trivialized the differential module with rank $r$. The $r$ columns $d\log t_i$ form a basis after the geometric residue-field extension, hence also over the residue field at its marked scheme point: the determinant of the square matrix is nonzero after that field extension if and only if it was nonzero before it. The module is already free of rank $r$, so [lem-weil-pbc-prescribed-residue-basis-spreads] applies to these prescribed columns and makes them a basis on a principal neighbourhood. This proves both the claimed stalk basis and its extension, with $t_i$ in the monoid itself, not merely its group completion.

source.place: Kato 3.13, p.204; Stacks Tag 0GWM, lemma-finitely-presented-localization-free, prescribed-basis form; ILO XVI 3.6.3 proof, p.252; precise Kato source WANTED locally, read online at https://math.uchicago.edu/~drinfeld/p-adic_periods/Kato_log-structures.pdf

proof.text: Finally suppose every test square has a unique global log lift. On any of the affine chart neighbourhoods of Step 5, use $J=W$ and the strict thickening $U\hookrightarrow T_W$ of Step 6. Its canonical map $c_W:T_W\to U\to X$ and the universal-derivation map $a_0:T_W\to U\to X$ are global lifts of the same map $U\to X$, over the same $T_W\to Y$. Uniqueness for the original $f$ makes them equal. Their difference is the identity of $W$ under Step 2, hence $\mathrm{id}_W=0$ and $W=0$. The local tensor models [lem-sfb-log-differential-finite-chart-model] cover $X$, so $\omega_f=0$. This argument uses uniqueness for the original test problems; it does not assume global lifts on a non-affine scheme merely from their local existence.
